chunks: Noah had verily called to Us. And how gracious was He who answered (him).
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God answering Noah's call?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah As-Saffat, this verse serves as a rhetorical affirmation of God's responsiveness, contrasting Noah's persistent call with the eventual acceptance of his prayer for deliverance. Shia exegetes often highlight this as a precedent for the efficacy of du'a even amidst prolonged trials, reinforcing the concept that divine response may come in the form of salvation from calamity rather than immediate worldly change. It underscores the attribute of 'Al-Mujib' (The Responder) not just as a passive listener, but as an active agent in the cosmic narrative of the prophets.
